thread:
Jess: Customer reported sudden 401s from long-running worker processes after we rotated API keys via Vault agent. Only affects their Python workers using multiprocessing with 'forkserver' start method.

Maya: Ok can you paste the minimal repro and the SDK version?

Jess: Repro steps from the customer:
1) Start app with Python multiprocessing start method 'forkserver' and spawn a pool of long-lived workers.
2) Client is created at module import time: 
```py
# some_module.py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['RW_API_KEY'], org=os.environ.get('RW_ORG'))
```
3) After some time they rotate the key via Vault agent writing a new env file and sending SIGHUP to the main process to reload env (they purposely do not restart workers).
4) Main process picks up new env and can make requests fine. Existing worker processes keep using the old in-memory client and start getting 401s.

Logs from worker: 
```
ERROR redwood.api - request failed 401 unauthorized - invalid_api_key
headers: {'authorization': 'Bearer sk_live_old...','x-org': 'org:abcd'}
```

Customer SDK version: 0.9.2. They said upgrading to 0.9.4 in a dev branch reduced occurrences but didn't fully solve.

Liam: That matches a class of bugs where we cache session/default headers on client init and the global HTTP session lives in worker memory. Forkserver will clone the memory at fork time; later env changes don't touch the cached header. If the server invalidates the old key, workers keep using it.

Anjali: Suggest immediate mitigation: 1) Lazy create clients inside the worker task (avoid module-level singletons), 2) use spawn start method so new workers pick up env, or 3) have a small signal handler in workers that calls client.reload_credentials(new_key) after main signals rotation.

Jess: Customer tried (1) and that worked but it's invasive to change app layout. They asked if we can add a helper to the SDK to detect env changes and refresh headers automatically.

Liam: We don't want the SDK to poll env continually. We can add an explicit refresh() method to the client that reloads api_key/org from os.environ and updates internal session headers atomically. That would be a small patch. Also add a note in docs for multiprocessing patterns.

Maya: Is there any security implication of auto-reloading from env? Vault agent rotates files; if someone spins up a new process with old file, weirdness can happen. Better to make behavior explicit: SDK will only refresh on calling client.refresh_from_env() or if client is created with refresh_on_signal=True and we listen for SIGHUP to refresh.

Liam: Agreed. I'll open an eng-runtime PR: add RedwoodClient.refresh_from_env(), also ensure headers are not shared via module-level global session by default (make a per-instance session or clone session headers on refresh). We'll mark this as patch for 0.9.5.

Anjali: I'll add a short note in the Multiprocessing troubleshooting doc and an example pattern (best practice: construct clients inside process or call client.refresh_from_env() after key rotation).

Jess: Customer accepted workaround (instantiate per-task) and asked for ETA on patch.

ops-bot: Deployed internal patch branch to staging for manual QA: branch "fix/refresh-from-env-0.9.5".

Liam: Follow-ups: I'll link PR and changelog here when open. Also add a unit test that simulates fork + env change and asserts refresh_from_env updates Authorization header.

Jess: Thanks team, I'll reply to customer with the workaround and ETA for 0.9.5.

Maya: One last note for triage - check interactions with our client caching in server frameworks (gunicorn preload, uwsgi) too; we saw similar but not identical reports.
